chords._schema: strings ordered low E (6) to high e (1). frets: null = muted/not played, 0 = open. fingers: 0 = open, 1 = index, 2 = middle, 3 = ring, 4 = pinky, null = muted.

exercises.name: Make the C shape
exercises.purpose: Land the C chord that walks up from G.

params.fingers: ring(3) on A 3rd fret, middle(2) on D 2nd fret, index(1) on B 1st fret, low E muted
params.strings_played: A, D, G, B, high e (low E stays quiet)

exercises.coaching: C steps up from G. Ring finger on the A string, third fret; middle on the D, second fret; index on the B, first fret; keep the low E quiet. That little triangle is the C chord — warm and open.

exercises.name: One clean down-strum
exercises.purpose: Strum the five ringing strings without catching the muted low E.

params.action: single downward strum, relaxed wrist, skip the low E
params.cue: listen for the open G string (the fifth) ringing

exercises.coaching: Hold C and strum down — but let the pick fall just past the low E so it stays silent. Loose wrist. Listen for the open G string; that's the fifth, the colour of the C chord. Buzz on the B or D? Press a touch closer to the fret. That clean C is the second colour of the country.

exercises.name: G to C walk
exercises.purpose: Practice the most common country change, slowly, in time.

params.cue: one chord per 4 beats, change on the downbeat

exercises.coaching: Now walk: G for four beats, C for four. One chord per four beats, change right on the click. The metronome is bright so you can land clean. This G-to-C move is in thousands of country tunes — you just met it.

avatar_coaching_copy.intro: Second colour of country: C. Small shape, but it walks you right out of G and into a real progression.
avatar_coaching_copy.ex1_intro: C is a triangle: ring on A third fret, middle on D second, index on B first, low E quiet. The open G is your fifth — that lift is the sound.
avatar_coaching_copy.ex2_intro: Strum down but let the pick fall past the low E so it stays silent. Loose wrist. Listen for the open G string. Buzz? Closer to the fret. That clean C is the second country colour.
avatar_coaching_copy.ex3_intro: Walk it: G four beats, C four beats, on the click. Bright metronome. That G-to-C move is in countless country songs — you just met it.
avatar_coaching_copy.results: If you can change G to C on the beat, you have the backbone of the style. Two colours down, one to go.
avatar_coaching_copy.wrap: G and C in your hands, walking in time. Lesson 3 of the pack adds D and you play a full I-IV-V change. For real.

lesson.title: Country Pack 2 — The C Chord (walking up from G)
lesson.one_line_promise: C + the G walk gives you the backbone of country.
objectives: Form C (ring A 3, middle D 2, index B 1, low E muted)
Strum it clean, skipping the muted low E
Walk G to C on the beat at a bright tempo

free_metronome: hold the G-C walk tempo (boom-chick feel)
